name: General Dynamics Corporation
industry: Aircraft, Guided Missile, and Space Vehicle Manufacturing

Defense budget appropriations cycle volatility; FY2025 continuing resolution delays impact contract award timing and cash-flow predictability.
Cybersecurity incident disclosure risk; defense contractors face elevated threat from state-sponsored actors targeting classified program data.
opportunitySignals: Hypersonic and directed-energy weapon platform acceleration; FY2025 DoD budget request includes 18% increase in advanced-propulsion R&D, favoring GD's Missiles and Fire Control segment.
International arms sales expansion; NATO allies' rearmament post-Ukraine drives demand for Gulfstream business jets and combat systems exports.
Space-based sensing and satellite constellation contracts; Space Systems Division positioned for multi-year NRO and Space Force awards in overhead reconnaissance.

Combat Systems — armored vehicles, turrets, fire-control systems
Technologies — advanced electronics, cybersecurity, autonomous systems
Aerospace — Gulfstream business jets, military transport aircraft

Aerospace revenue FY2023: $9.1B; Gulfstream G650/G700 deliveries and military variants

domainRelevance: General Dynamics is a Tier-1 prime contractor in U.S. defense, commanding ~$41B in annual revenue across missiles, combat systems, aerospace, and advanced technologies. The company holds critical positions in hypersonic weapons development, armored-vehicle production (M1 Abrams), and Gulfstream business-jet manufacturing—each a strategic asset in peer-competitor deterrence and allied interoperability. Its backlog-to-revenue ratio (4.0x+) and multi-decade program lifecycles (F-16 sustainment, Virginia-class submarine combat systems) anchor it as a structural beneficiary of sustained U.S. defense spending and NATO expansion.
portalRelevance: GD is a financial-intelligence anchor because its earnings, backlog, and margin trajectory are leading indicators of U.S. defense-industrial capacity, geopolitical risk appetite, and budget-cycle execution. Its supply-chain transparency (10-K Item 1A risk factors, quarterly earnings calls) reveals bottlenecks in advanced materials, electronics, and skilled labor that propagate across the entire defense-industrial base. As a mega-cap with $3.2B cash, $8.1B debt, and 0.78 composite health score, GD's capital allocation (dividends, buybacks, M&A) signals management confidence in sustained demand and provides a barometer for sector-wide capital discipline.

notes.cohortStatus: Tier-1 prime contractor; peer group includes Lockheed Martin (LMT), Northrop Grumman (NOC), Raytheon Technologies (RTX), Boeing (BA) defense segment

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Quarterly backlog announcements and contract wins (8-K filings, earnings releases); FY2024 YTD new awards $18.2B
Defense budget appropriations and continuing-resolution status; FY2025 DoD budget request $820B, GD-relevant categories (missiles, combat systems) +4-6% YoY
Supply-chain disruption notices and commodity price indices (aluminum, titanium, rare-earth elements); 2024 10-K discloses single-source dependencies in advanced electronics
Cybersecurity incident disclosures and regulatory filings (SEC Item 8-K, CISA advisories); GD classified-program environment subject to heightened threat reporting

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Kernel phase classification: p2 (stable, high-backlog, margin-expansion trajectory); 12-quarter rolling composite score 0.78 (green band)

Segment-level health: MFC (highest margin, 4.0x backlog multiple, hypersonic acceleration); Combat Systems (steady-state, Abrams sustainment); Aerospace (Gulfstream demand cyclical, military variants growth)
Cash-flow trajectory: operating cash flow FY2023 $5.1B; free cash flow $3.8B after capex; debt/EBITDA 2.1x (investment-grade)
Backlog composition: 85% U.S. government, 10% international allies, 5% commercial; multi-year contract visibility 4+ years

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Pattern match: GD exhibits classic p2 signature — high backlog, margin expansion, supply-chain stress, geopolitical tailwind. Comparable to 2015-2018 post-ISIS surge in MFC demand.
Risk signature: supply-chain concentration (Taiwan semiconductor, rare-earth processing); budget-cycle cliff risk if appropriations stall; cybersecurity breach risk in classified programs
Growth inflection: hypersonic and directed-energy weapon platforms entering production phase (2024-2026); international rearmament (NATO, Japan, South Korea) driving export acceleration
Competitive delta vs. LMT: GD stronger in combat systems and missiles; LMT stronger in space and integrated warfare systems; RTX dominant in propulsion and avionics

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Thesis: sustained defense spending (bipartisan consensus, NATO expansion, China/Russia deterrence) supports 4-6% annual revenue CAGR through 2028; margin expansion via operating leverage
Risk management: hedge supply-chain concentration via strategic inventory builds (titanium, rare-earth); diversify international customer base (NATO allies, Japan, South Korea, Australia)
Compliance monitoring: ITAR/EAR export controls, CFIUS foreign-investment reviews, FCPA anti-corruption (international sales); cybersecurity incident reporting (SEC Item 8-K, CISA)
Capital allocation: maintain investment-grade rating (debt/EBITDA <2.5x); prioritize organic R&D in hypersonic/directed-energy; selective M&A in advanced electronics and autonomous systems

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Long equity position: GD offers 4-6% annual dividend yield + 3-5% buyback yield; total shareholder return target 8-11% CAGR through 2027
Hedge: short-duration Treasury futures to hedge interest-rate sensitivity (GD debt refinancing risk); long volatility (VIX calls) to hedge geopolitical shock (Taiwan strait, Russia escalation)
Engagement: quarterly earnings-call monitoring for backlog growth, margin guidance, supply-chain commentary; annual 10-K deep-dive on Item 1A risks, customer concentration, contract terms

Portfolio positioning: overweight GD vs. LMT in tactical allocation; underweight vs. RTX on propulsion-cycle risk; monitor Boeing (BA) defense segment for competitive displacement in military transport

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Earnings validation: Q+1 same-store backlog growth, segment margin expansion, free-cash-flow conversion; compare guidance vs. prior-quarter outlook
Price reaction: monitor GD stock performance vs. defense-sector ETF (ITA, XAR) and vs. S&P 500; track implied volatility around earnings and budget-cycle events
Filing updates: 10-K Item 1A risk-factor changes (supply-chain, cybersecurity, budget); 8-K contract-award announcements; DEF14A executive compensation and board changes
Macro validation: track DoD budget appropriations, NATO defense spending, geopolitical risk indices (Russia/China tensions); correlate with GD backlog and order-intake trends

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Kernel reweighting: if hypersonic production ramps faster than modeled, increase MFC segment weight in composite score; if budget appropriations slip, reduce p2 phase confidence
Supply-chain sensitivity: quarterly recalibration of rare-earth and semiconductor dependency scores based on commodity prices and geopolitical risk (Taiwan strait, China export controls)
Competitive positioning: monitor LMT, NOC, RTX quarterly results for margin compression or backlog slowdown; adjust GD relative-value thesis if peer-group dynamics shift
Macro regime shift: if U.S. defense budget enters contraction (post-2028), downgrade GD to p3/p4 phase; if NATO expansion accelerates, upgrade to p1 (high-growth inflection)

functionalNetwork.model: General Dynamics operates as a distributed decision-making system across four semi-autonomous business segments (Missiles and Fire Control, Combat Systems, Aerospace, Technologies), each with distinct customer relationships, supply chains, and margin profiles. The company functions as a neural integrator between U.S. government procurement (DoD, intelligence agencies), allied defense ministries, and a global supply base of specialized materials and electronics suppliers. Its backlog-driven revenue model and multi-decade program lifecycles create a stable but geopolitically sensitive operating environment, requiring continuous monitoring of budget cycles, supply-chain bottlenecks, and cybersecurity threats.

suppliers.name: Raytheon Technologies Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: RTX supplies advanced propulsion systems, avionics, and integrated warfare components to GD's Aerospace and Combat Systems segments. FY2023 inter-company revenue estimated $1.2B+ (disclosed in 10-K Item 1 customer concentration). Strategic partnership in F-16 avionics upgrades and Virginia-class submarine combat systems integration; RTX Pratt & Whitney engines power Gulfstream G650/G700 variants.

suppliers.name: Boeing Defense, Space & Security
suppliers.relationshipNote: Boeing competes with GD in military transport aircraft (C-17, KC-46 tanker) and rotorcraft. GD's Aerospace segment (Gulfstream) does not directly compete with Boeing's commercial aircraft, but both pursue military variants and government contracts. FY2023 Boeing defense revenue ~$28B; GD Aerospace $9.1B. Boeing's 737 MAX and 787 supply-chain challenges create indirect competitive advantage for GD in military programs.

suppliers.name: Huntington Ingalls Industries Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: HII competes with GD in naval combat systems and submarine-integrated warfare. GD supplies combat systems to Virginia-class and Columbia-class submarines; HII builds the hulls and integrates systems. FY2023 HII revenue $9.5B; GD Combat Systems $6.8B. Complementary rather than direct competition; both benefit from Navy's submarine modernization (Columbia-class $128B program).

suppliers.name: Alcoa Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Alcoa supplies aerospace-grade aluminum alloys and forgings to GD's Aerospace segment (Gulfstream fuselage, wings) and Combat Systems (armored-vehicle components). FY2023 aerospace end-market revenue ~$3.2B for Alcoa; GD estimated 8-12% of Alcoa's aerospace volume. Strategic supplier for 2024-2026 Gulfstream G700 production ramp; subject to commodity-price volatility and supply-chain concentration risk.

suppliers.name: Titanium Metals Corporation (TIMET)
suppliers.relationshipNote: TIMET (subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway as of 2020) supplies titanium ingots, forgings, and fasteners to GD's Aerospace and Combat Systems segments. Titanium represents ~12-15% of Gulfstream airframe cost; critical for hypersonic missile bodies and armor applications. GD 10-K Item 1A flags titanium supply concentration risk; TIMET capacity constraints in 2023-2024 created production delays.

suppliers.name: Huntsman Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Huntsman supplies advanced composite resins, epoxies, and specialty chemicals to GD's Aerospace segment (Gulfstream composite structures) and Combat Systems (armor composites). FY2023 aerospace/defense end-market ~$1.8B for Huntsman; GD estimated 5-8% of volume. Strategic supplier for lightweight airframe and armor applications; subject to raw-material price volatility (petrochemicals).

suppliers.name: Anixter International (now part of Tech Data)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Tech Data (post-2021 Anixter merger) distributes advanced electronics, semiconductors, and IT components to GD's Technologies segment and Combat Systems. GD 10-K Item 1A discloses single-source dependencies in advanced semiconductors and rare-earth elements; Tech Data serves as critical distributor for supply-chain diversification.

suppliers.name: Precision Castparts Corp. (subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway)
suppliers.relationshipNote: PCC supplies precision investment castings, forgings, and fasteners to GD's Aerospace (Gulfstream engines, landing gear) and Combat Systems (turret mechanisms, hydraulic components). Acquired by Berkshire Hathaway in 2016 for $37.2B; critical supplier for high-reliability aerospace and defense applications. GD 10-K Item 1A flags supply-chain concentration in precision manufacturing.

logisticsPartners.name: DHL Supply Chain
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: DHL manages inbound logistics and supply-chain coordination for GD's Combat Systems and Missiles and Fire Control segments. Handles just-in-time delivery of components from global suppliers to manufacturing facilities in Lima (Ohio), St. Petersburg (Florida), and Scranton (Pennsylvania).

logisticsPartners.name: J.B. Hunt Transport Services
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: J.B. Hunt provides ground transportation and freight services for GD's Aerospace segment, including Gulfstream aircraft components and finished-goods delivery to customer sites. Defense-contractor logistics requires ITAR compliance and secure transportation; J.B. Hunt maintains cleared facilities and personnel.

logisticsPartners.name: Geodis (subsidiary of SNCF Logistics)
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Geodis manages international logistics and export compliance for GD's international arms sales (NATO allies, Japan, South Korea, Australia). Handles ITAR/EAR documentation, customs clearance, and secure delivery of combat systems and missiles. Critical for GD's international rearmament opportunity (FY2024 international orders +12% YoY).

logisticsPartners.name: Expeditors International of Washington Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Expeditors provides freight forwarding, customs brokerage, and supply-chain visibility for GD's global procurement and export operations. Manages inbound materials from Asia-Pacific suppliers (rare-earth elements, electronics) and outbound finished goods to international customers.

customers.name: U.S. Department of Defense
customers.relationshipNote: DoD accounts for ~85% of GD's FY2023 revenue ($34.9B of $41.0B). Primary customer for Missiles and Fire Control (hypersonic, air-defense systems), Combat Systems (M1 Abrams, armored vehicles), and Technologies (classified IT/cyber programs). Multi-decade program relationships: M1 Abrams sustainment ($2.1B annual), Virginia-class submarine combat systems ($1.8B annual), F-16 sustainment ($1.2B annual). Backlog $40B+ represents 4.0x revenue multiple.

customers.name: U.S. Intelligence Community (NSA, NRO, CIA)
customers.relationshipNote: GD's Technologies segment derives ~$1.2B annual revenue from classified intelligence programs (NRO satellite systems, NSA cybersecurity, CIA advanced analytics). Programs are multi-year, high-margin, and subject to security clearance and ITAR restrictions. GD maintains top-secret facility clearances at multiple locations; cybersecurity incident risk is elevated due to classified-program environment.

customers.name: NATO Allied Governments (Germany, UK, France, Poland, etc.)
customers.relationshipNote: NATO allies account for ~10% of GD's FY2023 revenue ($4.1B). Post-Ukraine rearmament (2022-2024) drove 18% YoY growth in international orders. Key programs: Gulfstream military variants (Germany, UK), combat systems (Poland, Czech Republic), missiles (NATO air-defense modernization). FY2024 international backlog growth +12% YoY; GD guidance projects international revenue to reach 15% by 2027.

customers.name: Japan Ministry of Defense
customers.relationshipNote: Japan is GD's largest Asia-Pacific customer, with FY2023 revenue ~$800M (combat systems, missiles, Gulfstream aircraft). Japan's 2023 defense budget increase (+5.5% to $51.4B) and 2024 strategic shift toward hypersonic/directed-energy weapons create multi-year growth opportunity. GD Missiles and Fire Control targeting $200M+ annual Japan revenue by 2027.

competitors.name: Lockheed Martin Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: LMT is GD's primary competitor across missiles, combat systems, and space. FY2023 LMT revenue $64.0B (vs. GD $41.0B); LMT stronger in space/satellites (Space Systems Division $12.8B), GD stronger in missiles/combat systems. Both compete for F-35 sustainment, hypersonic weapon development, and international arms sales. LMT's Missiles and Fire Control division revenue $11.2B (+4% YoY) vs. GD MFC $10.2B (+6% YoY); GD gaining share in hypersonic platforms.

competitors.name: Northrop Grumman Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: NOC competes with GD in integrated warfare systems, space-based sensing, and cybersecurity. FY2023 NOC revenue $36.8B; Aeronautics Systems division $8.2B (vs. GD Aerospace $9.1B). NOC stronger in space/satellites (Space Systems Division $7.1B), GD stronger in missiles/combat systems. Both pursue NRO satellite contracts and Space Force command-and-control systems. Occasional co-prime arrangements on large integrated programs.

competitors.name: Raytheon Technologies Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: RTX competes with GD in missiles, air-defense systems, and integrated warfare. FY2023 RTX revenue $67.0B; Missiles & Fire Control division $12.1B (vs. GD MFC $10.2B). RTX stronger in propulsion (Pratt & Whitney) and avionics; GD stronger in hypersonic platforms and combat systems. Both pursue DARPA hypersonic contracts and international air-defense modernization. RTX's 2024 guidance projects MFC revenue growth +5-7% YoY.

competitors.name: L3Harris Technologies Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: L3Harris competes with GD's Technologies segment in advanced electronics, cybersecurity, and classified IT programs. FY2023 L3Harris revenue $18.2B; Integrated Warfare Systems division $7.8B. L3Harris stronger in communications and electronic warfare; GD stronger in autonomous systems and directed-energy weapons. Both pursue DARPA and intelligence-community contracts. L3Harris 2024 guidance projects 3-4% revenue growth.

competitors.name: Huntington Ingalls Industries Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: HII competes with GD in naval combat systems and submarine-integrated warfare. FY2023 HII revenue $9.5B; Ingalls Shipbuilding division $5.2B. HII builds submarine hulls; GD supplies combat systems integration. Complementary rather than direct competition; both benefit from Navy's submarine modernization (Columbia-class $128B program, Virginia-class $120B+ program). HII 2024 guidance projects 4-5% revenue growth.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC regulates GD's public-company disclosures (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K filings). GD files annual 10-K with Item 1A risk factors (supply-chain concentration, cybersecurity, budget appropriations), Item 1B unresolved staff comments, Item 8 financial statements. GD's 2024 10-K (filed Feb 2024) disclosed $40B+ backlog, p2 phase classification, and elevated cybersecurity incident risk. SEC Form 8-K filings required for material contract awards and cybersecurity breaches.

regulators.name: U.S. Department of Defense (Contracting & Compliance)
regulators.relationshipNote: DoD contracting offices (DCMA, DFARS) oversee GD's contract performance, cost accounting, and compliance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS). GD maintains Cost Accounting Standards (CAS) compliance and undergoes annual DCAA audits. 2023 DoD audit findings:. GD's backlog is contingent on DoD budget appropriations and continuing-resolution status.

regulators.name: U.S. State Department (ITAR & Arms Control)
regulators.relationshipNote: State Department regulates GD's international arms sales via International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). GD's international revenue ($4.1B FY2023, 10% of total) requires State Department export licenses for combat systems, missiles, and Gulfstream military variants. GD 10-K Item 1A discloses ITAR compliance risk and geopolitical restrictions (China, Russia, Iran). 2024 NATO rearmament creates export-license acceleration opportunity.

regulators.name: U.S. Commerce Department (BIS & Export Control)
regulators.relationshipNote: Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) regulates GD's export of dual-use technologies (semiconductors, advanced electronics, software) via Export Administration Regulations (EAR). GD's Technologies segment ($3.9B FY2023) includes advanced electronics subject to EAR controls. GD 10-K Item 1A discloses China/Russia sanctions risk and supply-chain concentration in Taiwan semiconductors.

regulators.name: U.S. Federal Trade Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC monitors GD's competitive positioning and potential antitrust concerns. GD's 2023 acquisition of Hydra Technologies (advanced electronics, $ ) underwent FTC review. GD's combined market share with LMT, NOC, RTX in defense primes (~35% of U.S. defense spending) is subject to FTC scrutiny. No active FTC investigations disclosed in 2024 10-K.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte serves as GD's independent auditor (Big Four). FY2023 audit opinion: unqualified (clean). Deloitte audits GD's consolidated financial statements, internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR), and compliance with GAAP. Audit fees FY2023: $. Deloitte also provides tax and advisory services to GD (non-audit fees FY2023: $ ). Audit committee oversight: GD's board audit committee (3 independent directors) meets quarterly with Deloitte.

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan is GD's primary lender and investment banker. GD maintains $3.0B revolving credit facility with JPMorgan as administrative agent (maturity 2027). FY2023 borrowings: $. JPMorgan also manages GD's debt issuances (FY2023 bond issuance $2.5B, 10-year maturity, 4.85% coupon). JPMorgan equity research coverage: BUY rating, $290 price target (as of Q4 2024).

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Merrill Lynch
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: BofA Merrill Lynch is a syndicate lender on GD's $3.0B revolving credit facility and participates in debt issuances. BofA equity research coverage: BUY rating, $295 price target (as of Q4 2024). BofA also provides treasury management and foreign-exchange services to GD.

capitalProviders.name: Vanguard Group Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Vanguard is GD's largest institutional shareholder, holding ~7.2% of outstanding shares (as of Q4 2024). Vanguard's passive index funds (Vanguard Total Stock Market Index Fund, Vanguard Institutional Index Fund) hold GD as a core defense-sector position. Vanguard does not actively engage in GD governance but votes on board elections and executive compensation (DEF14A proxy).

capitalProviders.name: BlackRock Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: BlackRock is GD's second-largest institutional shareholder, holding ~6.8% of outstanding shares (as of Q4 2024). BlackRock's iShares U.S. Aerospace & Defense ETF (ITA) and core index funds hold GD as a major position. BlackRock engages with GD on ESG and governance issues (climate risk, board diversity, executive compensation). BlackRock's 2024 proxy voting: supported all GD board nominees and executive compensation.

executiveTeam.name: Phebe N. Novakovic
executiveTeam.title: Chief Executive Officer & Chairman
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Novakovic became CEO in 2013 and Chairman in 2015. Under her leadership, GD has executed strategic portfolio optimization (divested IT services, acquired Combat Systems), expanded backlog to $40B+, and increased dividend 8 consecutive years (2016-2024). FY2023 total compensation: $. Novakovic's 2024 guidance projects 4-6% annual revenue CAGR through 2027 and margin expansion via operating leverage.

executiveTeam.name: Jason F. Aiken
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Aiken became CFO in 2020. Responsible for GD's financial strategy, capital allocation, and investor relations. FY2023 free cash flow: $3.8B (up 6% YoY); debt/EBITDA: 2.1x (investment-grade). Aiken's 2024 guidance projects free cash flow growth +5-7% YoY and dividend increase +3-5% YoY. Total compensation FY2023: $.

executiveTeam.name: Frank Jimenez
executiveTeam.title: President & Chief Operating Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Jimenez became COO in 2021. Responsible for GD's operational execution across four business segments (MFC, Combat Systems, Aerospace, Technologies). Oversees supply-chain management, manufacturing efficiency, and program delivery. FY2023 operating margin: 12.1% (up 80 bps YoY). Jimenez's focus: supply-chain resilience, hypersonic production ramp, and international expansion.

executiveTeam.name: Kneeland A. Youngblood
executiveTeam.title: General Counsel & Secretary
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Youngblood serves as General Counsel and Secretary. Responsible for GD's legal strategy, regulatory compliance (ITAR, DFARS, FAR), and litigation management. GD's 2024 10-K discloses no material legal proceedings. Youngblood oversees GD's compliance with export controls, sanctions, and antitrust regulations.

marketSignals.name: Weekly Defense Spending Tracker (Bloomberg / Reuters)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Weekly tracking of DoD budget appropriations, continuing-resolution status, and contract award announcements. FY2025 DoD budget request: $820B (baseline) + $50B (supplemental for Ukraine/Taiwan). GD-relevant categories: Missiles & Fire Control (+6% YoY), Combat Systems (+4% YoY), Space Systems (+5% YoY). Continuing-resolution delays in 2024 created 2-3 week contract-award delays; full appropriations expected by Q1 2025.

marketSignals.name: Gulfstream Business Jet Demand Index (Honeywell / Textron)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Quarterly tracking of Gulfstream aircraft orders, backlog, and delivery rates. FY2023 Gulfstream revenue: $9.1B (+3% YoY); backlog: 8.2 years (vs. industry average 5-6 years). G700 production ramp accelerating (2024 target: 45 deliveries, +15% YoY). Commercial demand remains strong despite macro uncertainty; international military variants (NATO allies) driving incremental growth.

marketSignals.name: NATO Defense Spending Index (Stockholm International Peace Research Institute)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Annual tracking of NATO allies' defense spending. 2023 NATO defense spending: $1.24T (+5.1% YoY); 2024 projected: $1.32T (+6.5% YoY). Post-Ukraine rearmament (2022-2024) drove GD international revenue +18% YoY. Key drivers: Poland (+27% defense spending), Germany (+13%), UK (+8%). GD guidance projects international revenue to reach 15% of total by 2027 (vs. 10% FY2023).
